texts: Household Charge Payment: Pay the yearly household charge (the council bill for your home) online, by card or by bank transfer.
Household Charge Payment: Make a payment towards the household charge on your property and check the balance still owed.
Household Charge Payment: Paying the local council bill for a house or flat: one-off payments, paying the outstanding amount, or paying a reminder notice.
Ways to pay (Household Charge Payment): Pay the household charge by card online, by bank transfer, or by phone using the reference on your bill.
Check your balance (Household Charge Payment): See how much household charge is still owed for the current year and when the next instalment is due.
Reminder notices (Household Charge Payment): What a reminder or final notice means and how to bring payments up to date before further action is taken.
How to pay online (Household Charge Payment): Step-by-step guide to paying the household charge online with your account reference.
Household Charge Discounts: Reductions on the household charge depending on who lives in the property.
Household Charge Discounts: Single-occupier discount and other reductions on the household charge, for example when only one adult lives in a home, or for carers and people with a disability.
Household Charge Discounts: Lower the household charge bill when your circumstances mean you qualify for a reduction.
Discounts available (Household Charge Discounts): The household charge reductions available, such as the single-occupier discount and disability reductions.
Who qualifies (Household Charge Discounts): Conditions for each discount, including who counts as an adult living in the property.
How to claim a discount (Household Charge Discounts): How to apply for a household charge discount and what happens to your bill afterwards.
Telling us about changes (Household Charge Discounts): Report a change, such as someone moving in, that means a discount should stop.
Tax Records: Your household charge account history: past bills, payments and statements.
Tax Records: View household charge records for a property: previous bills, payment history and copies of old statements.
Tax Records: Get a copy of an earlier bill or proof of what was charged and paid on your home in a previous year.
Your account history (Tax Records): A list of household charge bills issued and payments received on your account.
Copies of bills (Tax Records): Request a duplicate of a previous household charge bill.
Proof of payment (Tax Records): Get confirmation of household charge paid, for example for a mortgage or tenancy application.
Payment Arrangements: Change how or when you pay the household charge.
Payment Arrangements: Spread the household charge across the year in instalments, move your payment date, or switch from yearly to monthly payments.
Payment Arrangements: Rearrange the timing of household charge payments to fit your pay day.
Instalment options (Payment Arrangements): Pay the household charge in ten or twelve monthly instalments, or in one payment.
Changing your payment date (Payment Arrangements): Move the date your instalment is collected each month.
How to request a change (Payment Arrangements): How to ask for a different payment arrangement and when it takes effect.
Exemptions: Properties and people that do not have to pay the household charge.

Exemptions: Find out whether a home is exempt from the household charge altogether, for example when everyone living there is studying on a qualifying course, or the property is empty for certain reasons.
Exemptions: Exemption from the local household charge for students, care leavers and some empty or uninhabitable homes.
Exemption types (Exemptions): The circumstances in which a property is fully exempt from the household charge.
Students and the household charge (Exemptions): How students on qualifying courses are treated and the proof of study needed.
Empty and uninhabitable homes (Exemptions): When an empty, repossessed or uninhabitable home does not have to pay.
How to apply for an exemption (Exemptions): How to claim an exemption and backdate it if you qualified earlier.
Annual Statements: Your yearly summary of household charges billed and paid.
Annual Statements: The annual statement summarising the household charge billed, discounts applied and payments made over the year.
Annual Statements: A year-end summary of the amounts billed and received on the household charge account for a property.
Reading your statement (Annual Statements): What each line of the annual household charge statement means.
Download a statement (Annual Statements): Download or print the statement for the current or a previous year.
Statement queries (Annual Statements): What to do if a payment is missing from your statement.
Charge Appeals: Challenge your household charge if the bill or the valuation band is wrong.
Charge Appeals: Appeal against the household charge when you believe the property has been put in the wrong valuation band or the bill has been calculated incorrectly.
Charge Appeals: Dispute the band or amount of the council charge on your home and ask for it to be reviewed.
Grounds for appeal (Charge Appeals): Reasons you can challenge a household charge, such as the wrong band or wrong liability.
Valuation bands (Charge Appeals): How properties are placed in valuation bands and how a band can be reviewed.
How to appeal (Charge Appeals): How to lodge a household charge appeal and the time limits.
What happens next (Charge Appeals): How long an appeal takes and what to pay while it is considered.
Direct Debit: Pay the household charge automatically from your bank account.
Direct Debit: Set up, change or cancel a direct debit so the household charge is collected automatically each month.
Direct Debit: Automatic payment of the council bill for your home from your bank account.
Set up a direct debit (Direct Debit): Set up a direct debit for the household charge using your bank details.
Change bank details (Direct Debit): Update the account your direct debit is collected from.
Cancel a direct debit (Direct Debit): Stop a direct debit, for example when you move out of a property.
Household Support: Help with essential household items when you cannot afford them.
Household Support: Help getting essential household goods such as a bed, cooker, fridge or washing machine if you are setting up home or cannot afford to replace them.
Household Support: One-off support with furniture and white goods for people on a low income or moving out of temporary housing.
Items we can help with (Household Support): Essential furniture and appliances that can be provided or paid for.
Who can get household support (Household Support): Eligibility for help with household items, based on income and circumstances.
How to ask for help (Household Support): How to request household support and how items are delivered.
Emergency Assistance: Urgent crisis help when you have no money for essentials right now.
Emergency Assistance: Crisis support when you cannot pay for food, gas or electricity today, including food bank referrals and emergency top-ups for prepayment meters.
Emergency Assistance: Same-day emergency help in a financial crisis, for example after losing a purse, a delayed payment or a sudden emergency.
Crisis help available (Emergency Assistance): Food vouchers, energy top-ups and emergency payments for urgent needs.
Who can get emergency help (Emergency Assistance): When you can get crisis support and how often.
How to get help today (Emergency Assistance): How to ask for emergency assistance quickly, by phone or online.
Food banks (Emergency Assistance): How food bank referrals work and where local food banks are.
Care Support Payment: A regular payment towards the extra costs of disability or long-term illness.
Care Support Payment: A payment to help with the additional living costs of a long-term health condition or disability.
Care Support Payment: Financial support for people whose illness or disability means they need extra help day to day.
What the payment covers (Care Support Payment): The extra costs the care support payment is meant to help with.
Who can claim (Care Support Payment): Health conditions and care needs that may qualify.
How to claim (Care Support Payment): How to start a claim and the medical evidence that helps.
Payment rates (Care Support Payment): How much the care support payment is and how often it is paid.
Eligibility Checker: Find out which benefits and support you might be entitled to.
Eligibility Checker: Answer a few questions about your household, income and circumstances to see which benefits and support payments you could claim.
Eligibility Checker: Check your entitlement to financial help before applying, for example when working on a low income or after a change in circumstances.
Start the checker (Eligibility Checker): Use the online checker to estimate the support you might qualify for.
Information you need (Eligibility Checker): Details about income, savings, rent and household members to have ready.
Understanding your results (Eligibility Checker): What the checker results mean and how to apply for each type of support.
Support Applications: Track or manage a support application you have already made.
Support Applications: Follow the progress of a benefit or support claim you have submitted and see if anything else is needed from you.
Check your application (Support Applications): See the status of a support application and the date it was received.
Send more information (Support Applications): Upload extra information requested about your claim.
Processing times (Support Applications): How long support applications usually take to be decided.
Evidence Requirements: Which evidence and documents are accepted for support claims.
Evidence Requirements: The proof needed to support a benefit claim, such as payslips, bank statements, tenancy agreements and identity documents.
Evidence Requirements: What documents to provide to show your income, savings and housing costs when applying for support.
Proof of income (Evidence Requirements): Accepted evidence of earnings and other income, such as payslips and pension statements.
Proof of identity and address (Evidence Requirements): Documents accepted to confirm who you are and where you live.
How to send evidence (Evidence Requirements): Upload, post or bring in documents, and how originals are returned.
Payment Information: Dates, amounts and changes to support payments you already receive.
Payment Information: When benefit and support payments are paid into your account, how much you receive and why an amount might change.
Payment Information: Payment schedule and bank holiday changes for support payments.
Payment dates (Payment Information): The day support payments are made and changes around bank holidays.
Payment amounts (Payment Information): How your payment amount is worked out and why it can change.
Missing payments (Payment Information): What to do if a support payment has not arrived.
Change your bank account (Payment Information): Update the bank account your support is paid into.
Appeals: Appeal a benefit or support decision you disagree with.
Appeals: Ask for a benefit or support decision to be looked at again if a claim was refused, a payment was stopped or the amount awarded seems wrong.
Appeals: Dispute a decision about your benefits through a reconsideration and then an independent appeal.
Ask for a reconsideration (Appeals): Request that a support decision is looked at again before appealing.
Appeal to a tribunal (Appeals): How to take a benefit decision to an independent tribunal.
Time limits (Appeals): Deadlines for challenging a support decision.
Getting advice (Appeals): Free help preparing a benefits appeal.
Support Reviews: Reviews of support you already receive, and reporting changes.
Support Reviews: Scheduled reviews of an existing award and how to report a change in your circumstances, such as a new job, a new partner or moving home.
When reviews happen (Support Reviews): How often support awards are reviewed and what is checked.
Report a change (Support Reviews): Tell us about changes in income, household or address that affect your support.
After a review (Support Reviews): What happens if your support goes up, down or stops after a review.
Housing Repairs: Repairs in rented homes: getting a landlord to fix broken heating, boilers, leaks, damp, mould, windows or electrics.
Housing Repairs: What to do when something in your rented flat or house is broken and needs repairing.
Housing Repairs: Tenants' rights to repairs and what a landlord is responsible for maintaining.
What counts as a repair (Housing Repairs): What counts as a repair, from broken fixtures to faults with heating, water or wiring.

What your landlord must fix (Housing Repairs): Which repairs a landlord is legally responsible for, such as the structure, heating, hot water, gas, drains and electrics, and which are the tenant's job.
How to report a repair (Housing Repairs): How to report a repair to your landlord or housing provider, and what to include.
If repairs are not done (Housing Repairs): What to do if a landlord ignores repair requests or does not respond, including asking the council to inspect and take action.
Rent Support: Help paying your rent on a low income or if you have fallen behind.
Rent Support: Financial help with rent for tenants on a low income, including discretionary payments and help with rent arrears.
Rent Support: Support for renters who cannot cover the full rent, for example after a drop in income.
Help with rent costs (Rent Support): Types of rent support, including help towards ongoing rent and one-off payments.
Rent arrears (Rent Support): What to do if you owe rent and how to avoid eviction.
How to apply for rent support (Rent Support): How to apply and the evidence of rent and income needed.
Property Records: Official records about a property.
Property Records: Records about a property such as ownership history, boundaries, official addresses and land details.
Ownership information (Property Records): How to find out who owns a property or piece of land.
Boundaries and plans (Property Records): Records of property boundaries and site plans.
Request a property record (Property Records): How to request copies of property records and any fees.
Tenancy Support: Advice on your rights as a tenant.
Tenancy Support: Advice for tenants about eviction notices, deposits, tenancy agreements, rent increases and disputes with a landlord.
Tenancy Support: Help when a landlord is ending a tenancy, withholding a deposit or not following the rules.
Your rights as a tenant (Tenancy Support): The main rights and responsibilities of tenants and landlords.
Notices and eviction (Tenancy Support): What an eviction notice means and the steps a landlord must follow.
Deposits (Tenancy Support): How tenancy deposits must be protected and how to get yours back.
Get tenancy advice (Tenancy Support): Contact a tenancy adviser for help with a dispute.
Housing Applications: Apply for social housing through the housing register.
Housing Applications: Join the housing register to be considered for a council or housing association home, and check your place and banding.
Housing Applications: Applying for affordable social rented housing when you need a more suitable home.
Who can apply (Housing Applications): Who can join the housing register and how priority is decided.
How to join the register (Housing Applications): How to make a housing application and the information needed.
Bidding for homes (Housing Applications): How available social homes are advertised and how to bid.
Your application status (Housing Applications): Check your banding and position on the register.
Neighbourhood Issues: Problems with neighbours and antisocial behaviour.
Neighbourhood Issues: Report problems with neighbours such as persistent noise, antisocial behaviour, nuisance or disputes, and get help with mediation.
Neighbourhood Issues: Support when life at home is being disrupted by people living nearby.
Noise nuisance (Neighbourhood Issues): How to report ongoing noise from a neighbouring home and how it is investigated.
Antisocial behaviour (Neighbourhood Issues): Report intimidation, harassment or other antisocial behaviour near your home.
Mediation (Neighbourhood Issues): Free mediation to help resolve disputes between neighbours.
Property Information: General information about homes and their features.
Property Information: Information about a home such as its energy rating, council tax band, flood risk and nearby services.
Energy ratings (Property Information): What a home energy rating shows and how to improve it.
Flood risk (Property Information): Check the flood risk for a property.
Local services (Property Information): Schools, transport and services near a property.
Housing Costs: Understanding the costs of housing.
Housing Costs: Information on housing costs such as service charges, ground rent, shared ownership and affordability.
Service charges (Housing Costs): What service charges in flats cover and how to question them.
Shared ownership (Housing Costs): How part-buy, part-rent homes work.
Affordability (Housing Costs): Working out what housing you can afford.
Temporary Accommodation: Emergency and temporary housing if you are homeless or about to be.
Temporary Accommodation: Emergency and temporary accommodation if you are homeless, have been told to leave your home, or have nowhere safe to sleep tonight.
Temporary Accommodation: Help when you are about to lose your home, including domestic abuse and sudden homelessness.
Homeless tonight (Temporary Accommodation): What to do if you have nowhere to sleep tonight, including out-of-hours help.
Threatened with homelessness (Temporary Accommodation): Help to prevent homelessness if you have been asked to leave.
What temporary accommodation is like (Temporary Accommodation): The types of temporary housing offered and how long stays usually last.
Apply for homelessness help (Temporary Accommodation): How to make a homelessness application.
Housing Appeals: Ask for a review of a housing decision.
Housing Appeals: Request a review of a housing decision, such as your housing register banding, a homelessness decision or the suitability of an offer of accommodation.
Decisions you can challenge (Housing Appeals): Housing decisions that can be reviewed.
How to request a review (Housing Appeals): How to ask for a housing review and the time limit.
After the review (Housing Appeals): What happens if the decision is changed or confirmed.
Residential Parking: A residents' parking permit so you can park your car on the street near your home.
Residential Parking: Permission to park outside or close to your house in a controlled parking zone, including after moving to a new address.
Eligibility (Residential Parking): Who can get a residents' parking permit, based on address and vehicle.
Permit requirements (Residential Parking): What you need to apply for a parking permit, such as proof of address and vehicle details.
Permit charges (Residential Parking): How much a residential parking permit costs each year, what residents pay to park near their home, and the price of different permit lengths.
How to apply (Residential Parking): How to apply for a residents' parking permit online.
Visitor Parking: Parking permits for visitors, family, friends or tradespeople coming to your home.
Visitor Parking: Short-term permits so guests, relatives or a builder can park in a residents-only zone while they are with you.
Eligibility (Visitor Parking): Who can buy visitor permits for guests.
Visitor permits (Visitor Parking): How to get and use visitor parking permits.
Charges (Visitor Parking): How much visitor parking permits cost.
Vehicle Registration: Register a car, van or motorbike you have bought, or update the registered keeper details.
Vehicle Registration: Vehicle registration and the yearly vehicle charges you owe for a car or motorcycle.
Who can register (Vehicle Registration): Who can register a vehicle and be its registered keeper.
Information required (Vehicle Registration): Documents and vehicle details you need in order to register.
Registration process (Vehicle Registration): The step-by-step process to register a vehicle.
Fees and charges (Vehicle Registration): The registration fee and annual vehicle charges you owe for a car, van or motorbike.
Road Permits: Permits for placing things on or using the public road during works.
Road Permits: Permission to place a builder's skip, scaffolding, a crane or building materials on the highway, or to occupy the road while work is carried out.
Road Permits: Licences for temporary use of the street or pavement by builders, removal firms and contractors.
Permits you may need (Road Permits): Which works and equipment on the highway need a permit, such as skips, scaffolding and hoardings.
Permit fees (Road Permits): How much road and highway permits cost and how long they last.
How to apply for a road permit (Road Permits): How to apply, how much notice is needed and the safety conditions.
Public Transport: Local buses, trains and community transport.
Public Transport: Local bus and train routes, timetables, bus stops and community transport, and how to give feedback about a service.
Public Transport: Getting around by public transport and reporting problems with unreliable or cancelled routes.
Routes and timetables (Public Transport): Find local bus and train routes and timetables.
Community transport (Public Transport): Dial-a-ride and community minibus services for people who cannot use regular buses.
Feedback on services (Public Transport): Report problems with a bus route, a damaged bus shelter or a service that does not run as timetabled.
Road Services: Report and track problems with roads, pavements and streetlights.
Road Services: Report potholes, damaged roads, broken streetlights, blocked drains and uneven or broken pavements.
Road Services: Road maintenance: repairs to carriageways and footways, winter gritting and roadside drainage.
Report a road defect (Road Services): Report a pothole, sunken road surface or damaged kerb.
Streetlights and signs (Road Services): Report a streetlight that is out or a damaged road sign.
Claims for damage (Road Services): How to claim if your vehicle was damaged by a road defect.
Gritting and drainage (Road Services): Winter gritting routes and blocked roadside drains.
Vehicle Records: Records about a vehicle's history and keepers.
Vehicle Records: Records of a vehicle's history, previous keepers, registration documents and any outstanding notices.
Vehicle history (Vehicle Records): Check the recorded history of a vehicle.
Registration documents (Vehicle Records): Request a copy of a vehicle registration document.
Keeper records (Vehicle Records): Records of previous and current registered keepers.
Parking Charges: Tariffs for public council car parks and pay-and-display bays, and paying or disputing a parking fine (penalty charge notice).
Parking Charges: Charges for council car parks and pay-and-display bays, and how to pay or challenge a parking fine or penalty charge notice.
Parking Charges: Parking tickets and penalty charges: paying, appealing and what happens if you ignore one.
Car park tariffs (Parking Charges): What it costs to park in council car parks and on-street pay-and-display bays.
Pay a parking fine (Parking Charges): Pay a penalty charge notice online or by phone.
Challenge a parking fine (Parking Charges): How to challenge a penalty charge notice you think was wrongly issued.
Travel Support: Free or discounted travel for older people, disabled people and young people.
Travel Support: Free or reduced-fare bus passes for older people and disabled people, travel help for young people and companion passes.
Travel Support: Concessionary travel and blue badges for people with mobility difficulties.
Bus passes (Travel Support): Who can get a free or discounted bus pass and how to apply.
Blue badges (Travel Support): Parking concessions for people with severe mobility problems.
Travel help for young people (Travel Support): Discounted travel for children, students and young people.
Renew or replace a pass (Travel Support): Renew an expiring pass or replace a lost one.
Traffic Reports: Roadworks, closures and traffic disruption.
Traffic Reports: Current and planned roadworks, road closures, diversions and traffic disruption in the area.
Current roadworks (Traffic Reports): Roadworks happening now and expected finish dates.
Planned closures (Traffic Reports): Upcoming road closures and diversions.
Report a traffic problem (Traffic Reports): Report faulty traffic lights or a dangerous junction.
Development Approval: Find out whether you need planning permission or approval to build an extension, loft conversion, conservatory, garage or extra storey on your home.
Development Approval: Development approval before making your house bigger or altering a building.
Development Approval: Rules for building work on your property and how to get permission before work starts.
Do I need approval? (Development Approval): Whether your building project needs approval or is allowed without permission.
Application types (Development Approval): The different types of development application.
Documents (Development Approval): Plans and documents to submit with a development application.
Fees (Development Approval): How much a development application costs.
Decision process (Development Approval): How and when a decision on a development application is made.
Planning Applications: Search, view and comment on planning applications.
Planning Applications: Look up planning applications in your area, see the drawings, and support or raise objections to proposed building work before a decision is made.
Planning Applications: Have your say on development near you: comment on applications from neighbours, developers or businesses.
Search applications (Planning Applications): Find planning applications by address, street or reference number.
Comment on an application (Planning Applications): How to support or object to a planning application and the deadline for comments.
How decisions are made (Planning Applications): How planning applications are assessed and who decides them.
Weekly lists (Planning Applications): New applications received and decisions issued each week.
Building Guidance: Building regulations guidance for safe construction.
Building Guidance: Building regulations: structural safety, fire safety, insulation and inspections for building work, and when you need building control approval.
Building Guidance: Technical guidance for builders and homeowners carrying out structural alterations.
When building regulations apply (Building Guidance): Types of work that need building regulations approval.
Inspections (Building Guidance): Site inspections during building work and completion certificates.
Using an approved inspector (Building Guidance): Choosing between council building control and an approved inspector.
Property Development: Guidance for larger developments and commercial building projects.
Property Development: Guidance for developers on major developments, new housing estates and commercial building schemes, including pre-application advice.
Pre-application advice (Property Development): Paid advice for developers before submitting a major application.
Developer contributions (Property Development): Contributions developers make towards local infrastructure.
Major application process (Property Development): How large-scale applications are handled.
Local Plans: The long-term plan for where new homes, shops and roads will go.
Local Plans: The local plan setting out where new homes, jobs, shops and roads are planned over the coming years, and consultations on it.
The current local plan (Local Plans): Read the adopted local plan and its maps.
Plan consultations (Local Plans): Have your say on a draft local plan.
Site allocations (Local Plans): Land identified for future housing and employment.
Planning Records: Records of past planning decisions for a property.
Planning Records: Historic planning decisions, approvals and conditions attached to a property or site.
Search past decisions (Planning Records): Find previous planning decisions for an address.
Planning conditions (Planning Records): Conditions attached to past approvals.
Request copies (Planning Records): Request copies of older planning documents.
Development Fees: Fees for planning and development applications.
Development Fees: Fees charged for planning applications, building control and related development services.
Planning application fees (Development Fees): The fee for each type of planning application.
Building control charges (Development Fees): Charges for building regulations applications and inspections.
Paying fees (Development Fees): How to pay application fees and when refunds apply.
Application Guidance: Help preparing a planning application.
Application Guidance: How to prepare a planning application: drawings, location plans, forms and supporting documents.
Plans and drawings (Application Guidance): The plans and drawings an application needs.
Supporting documents (Application Guidance): Reports that may be required, such as heritage or tree surveys.
Common mistakes (Application Guidance): Reasons applications are returned as invalid.
Planning Appeals: Appeal against a refused planning application.
Planning Appeals: Appeal when planning permission has been refused or granted with conditions you disagree with, or when no decision was made in time.
Planning Appeals: Take a planning refusal to an independent inspector.
When you can appeal (Planning Appeals): Decisions that can be appealed and who can appeal.
How to appeal (Planning Appeals): How to submit a planning appeal and the time limits.
Appeal outcomes (Planning Appeals): What happens when an appeal is allowed or dismissed.
Neighbourhood Development: Community-led neighbourhood plans and regeneration.
Neighbourhood Development: Neighbourhood plans written by local communities and regeneration projects in town centres and estates.
Neighbourhood plans (Neighbourhood Development): How communities can write a neighbourhood plan.
Regeneration projects (Neighbourhood Development): Current regeneration schemes and their progress.
Get involved (Neighbourhood Development): How residents can take part in shaping their area.
Business Licence: Licences to run a business, sell food or alcohol, or trade in the street.
Business Licence: Licences needed to run certain businesses: selling alcohol, street trading, market stalls, mobile catering, taxis and entertainment.
Business Licence: Permission to trade from a stall, van or temporary pitch, and premises licences for cafés, bars and takeaways.
Which licence you need (Business Licence): Find which licence applies to your type of business or activity.
Street trading and markets (Business Licence): Licences for street trading, market pitches and mobile food units.
Licence fees (Business Licence): How much each business licence costs.
How to apply for a licence (Business Licence): How to apply, the checks involved and how long it takes.
Trading Registration: Register a new business or food business before you start trading.
Trading Registration: Register a food business, home bakery or catering business with the council before trading, and arrange a hygiene inspection.
Trading Registration: Formal registration steps when setting up a new business locally.
Who must register (Trading Registration): Businesses that must register with the council, including food businesses run from home.
Food hygiene inspections (Trading Registration): How hygiene inspections and ratings work.
How to register (Trading Registration): Register your business online before you open.
Employment Support: Help finding work and building skills for a job.
Employment Support: Support to find a job, including careers advice, CV help, job clubs and help returning to work after illness, caring or time away.
Employment Support: Employment programmes for people who are out of work or want to change job.
Job search help (Employment Support): CV writing, interview practice and job clubs.
Returning to work (Employment Support): Support for people coming back to work after a long gap, ill health or caring.
Training for work (Employment Support): Free short courses that lead to jobs.
Business Rates: Business rates bills, payments and relief for commercial premises.
Business Rates: Business rates on shops, offices, units and other commercial property: how the bill is worked out, paying it and rate relief for small businesses.
How rates are calculated (Business Rates): How the rateable value and multiplier set your business rates bill.
Rate relief (Business Rates): Small business and other reliefs that reduce the bill.
Pay business rates (Business Rates): Ways to pay your business rates bill.
Local Business Support: Grants, advice and support to start or grow a business.
Local Business Support: Advice, workshops, grants and mentoring for people starting a business or growing a small firm.
Starting a business (Local Business Support): Free advice for new entrepreneurs.
Business grants (Local Business Support): Grants available to local businesses.
Networking and mentoring (Local Business Support): Business networks and mentoring schemes.
Trading Standards: Consumer protection and reporting unfair traders.
Trading Standards: Consumer protection: report a trader who sold faulty or counterfeit goods, refused a refund you were owed, or used scams or misleading pricing.
Trading Standards: Your consumer rights when goods or services are not as described, and investigations into rogue traders and doorstep crime.
Your consumer rights (Trading Standards): Rights to a repair, replacement or refund when goods are faulty or not as described.
Report a trader (Trading Standards): Report a business for unfair trading, counterfeit goods or scams.
Doorstep crime (Trading Standards): Protecting older and vulnerable people from rogue traders.
Product safety (Trading Standards): Unsafe products and age-restricted sales.
Workplace Guidance: Health and safety at work and employment rights guidance.
Workplace Guidance: Guidance on health and safety at work and employment rights for workers and employers.
Health and safety (Workplace Guidance): Workplace safety duties and reporting accidents.
Employment rights (Workplace Guidance): Basic rights on pay, hours and holidays.
Report an unsafe workplace (Workplace Guidance): Raise a concern about safety at a workplace.
Business Records: Records about registered businesses and licences.
Business Records: Public registers of licensed and registered businesses, and records of licences issued.
Public registers (Business Records): Search registers of licensed premises and businesses.
Licence records (Business Records): Records of licences issued, renewed or revoked.
Request business records (Business Records): How to request copies of business records.
Licensing Appeals: Appeal a decision to refuse or revoke a licence.
Licensing Appeals: Challenge a decision to refuse, restrict or revoke a business, premises or trading licence.
Decisions you can appeal (Licensing Appeals): Licensing decisions that can be challenged.
How to appeal (Licensing Appeals): How to appeal to the magistrates or the licensing committee.
Time limits (Licensing Appeals): Deadlines for licensing appeals.
Business Premises: Find or rent commercial premises.
Business Premises: Find shops, offices, workshops and business units to rent, including council-owned premises.
Available premises (Business Premises): Council-owned business units available to rent.
Renting a unit (Business Premises): Leases, deposits and costs of renting premises.
Change of use (Business Premises): When using premises for a new purpose needs permission.
School Place: Apply for a place at a primary or secondary school.
School Place: Apply for a school place for your child when they start primary school, move up to secondary school, or need to change school after moving house.
School Place: School admissions: choosing schools, application deadlines and in-year transfers.
Starting primary school (School Place): How and when to apply for a reception place.
Moving to secondary school (School Place): Applying for a secondary school place and national offer day.
Changing school during the year (School Place): In-year applications when you move to a new area or need a different school.
How places are offered (School Place): Admission criteria such as catchment areas and siblings.
Childcare Support: Finding and paying for childcare.
Childcare Support: Free childcare hours, help with nursery and childminder costs, and finding registered childcare for babies, toddlers and pre-school children.
Childcare Support: Support with the cost of early years care so parents can work or study.
Free childcare hours (Childcare Support): Funded hours for eligible two-, three- and four-year-olds.
